record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: Does every homogeneous structure that has finite big Ramsey degrees also carry a big Ramsey structure, and is there an exact correspondence between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics analogous to the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence? The desired correspondence would give a dynamical understanding of big Ramsey degrees comparable to the known dynamical characterization for finite small Ramsey degrees.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Does every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees also carry a big Ramsey structure? Is there an exact correspondence, in the vein of the KPT-correspondence, between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics?
The hope in Problem 6.3 is to obtain as complete a dynamical understanding of big Ramsey degrees as we have for small Ramsey degrees

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let L be a countable first-order language and let K be a Fraïssé class of finite L-structures with Fraïssé limit F (i.e., F is the unique up to isomorphism countable, locally finite, ultrahomogeneous L-structure whose age is K). For a finite substructure A of F and another finite substructure B of F, write \binom{F}{A} for the set of all isomorphic copies of A in F. The big Ramsey degree T(A,F) of A in F is the least natural number t (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring c of \binom{F}{A} there is a copy F' of F inside F with c assuming at most t values on \binom{F'}{A}. F is said to have finite big Ramsey degrees if T(A,F) < ∞ for every finite A ≤ F.

A big Ramsey structure for F is an expansion F^* of F in a (possibly enriched) language such that:
(i) the age K^* of F^* is a "precompact" Ramsey expansion of K capturing the big Ramsey degrees, in the sense that for each finite A ≤ F the number of expansions of A appearing in F^* equals T(A,F); and
(ii) the expansion is "canonical" so that the topological group Aut(F^*) acts on the space of all expansions of F by copies of F^* in a way that mirrors the Kechris–Pestov–Todorcevic (KPT) framework. (KPT theorem: a Fraïssé class K with Fraïssé limit F has finite small Ramsey degrees iff the universal minimal flow of Aut(F) is metrizable; precompact expansions with the Ramsey property correspond bijectively to metrizable universal minimal flows arising as the closure of the orbit of the generic expansion.)

Problem. (a) Does every homogeneous (Fraïssé limit) structure F with finite big Ramsey degrees admit a big Ramsey structure in the sense above?

(b) Establish an exact correspondence, analogous to the KPT-correspondence for small Ramsey degrees, between big Ramsey structures of F and a suitable class of dynamical objects associated with Aut(F), yielding a dynamical characterization of finiteness of big Ramsey degrees that is as complete as the KPT characterization of finiteness of small Ramsey degrees.
artifact.category_tag: Big Ramsey degrees and topological dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees carries a big Ramsey structure, together with an exact KPT-style dynamical correspondence for big Ramsey degrees, remains an active open problem. Partial results have been obtained (e.g., big Ramsey structures are known for many binary FAP/SAP homogeneous structures and recently for the universal 3-uniform hypergraph and the K_4-free graph), but no general theorem establishing the correspondence is known.
